name: Boeing 737
engines: 2 jet engines under the wings; engine intakes are flattened at the bottom (oval, not round)
features: Pointed nose, winglets (upturned or split-scimitar tips on newer models), low wings, 2 engines. Very common short-haul jet. Engines sit close to the ground.
airlines: Southwest, Ryanair, United, Alaska, Delta, American, Jet2, Qantas

name: Airbus A320 family
engines: 2 jet engines under the wings; round intakes
features: Rounder, slightly blunter nose than a 737, sharklets (big upturned wingtip fences) on newer ones, 2 engines. Most common short-haul jet in Europe.
airlines: easyJet, Lufthansa, JetBlue, Spirit, Frontier, Wizz Air, Air France, IndiGo

name: Boeing 747
engines: 4 jet engines, 2 under each wing
features: Distinctive hump on the front of the fuselage (upper deck). Very large. Now mostly cargo, with a few passenger ones (Lufthansa 747-8).
airlines: Lufthansa, UPS, FedEx, Atlas Air, Korean Air Cargo, Air Force One

name: Airbus A380
size: the largest passenger plane, double-deck full length
engines: 4 jet engines, 2 under each wing
features: Full-length double-decker fuselage with a bulbous, whale-like look from the front. Gigantic wings. Rare and unmistakable.
airlines: Emirates, Singapore Airlines, Qantas, British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar

name: Boeing 777
engines: 2 enormous jet engines, one under each wing; 6 wheels per main landing gear
features: Giant engines for a twin, long body, 6-wheel main gear bogies, raked wingtips (no winglets) on most. Long-haul workhorse. Newer 777X has folding wingtips.
airlines: Emirates, Qatar, United, Cathay Pacific, Air France, British Airways

name: Boeing 787 Dreamliner
engines: 2 jet engines with zigzag/sawtooth (chevron) edges on the back of the nacelles
features: Very curved, flexing wings that bend upward in flight, raked wingtips, sawtooth engine nacelle edges, smooth nose with a swooping windshield. Long-haul.
airlines: ANA, JAL, British Airways, United, American, Qatar, Norse

name: Airbus A350
engines: 2 jet engines
features: Black 'mask' around the cockpit windows that joins into a swoosh, curved winglets blending into the wing, sleek fuselage. Long-haul twin.
airlines: Singapore, Qatar, Cathay Pacific, Finnair, Delta, Lufthansa, Air France

name: Airbus A330
engines: 2 jet engines
features: Wide-body twin, wingtips with winglets angled up and down (not raked). Looks like a bigger A320 with 2 aisles. Often seen on medium and long routes.
airlines: Delta, TAP, Turkish, Air Canada, Qantas

name: Boeing 767
engines: 2 jet engines
features: Smaller wide-body twin with a narrower fuselage than a 777, often cargo. 'Cheek' bulge near cockpit. Common as FedEx/UPS/Amazon freighters.
airlines: FedEx, UPS, Amazon Air, Delta, United, Air Canada

name: Embraer E175 / E190 regional jet
engines: 2 jet engines under the wings, close to the fuselage
features: Short, stubby, small airliner with winglets, 2 engines under wings. Common US regional jet flown for the big airlines.
airlines: SkyWest (for United/Delta/American), Republic, KLM Cityhopper, LOT

name: Bombardier CRJ-200 / CRJ-700 regional jet
engines: 2 jet engines mounted on the rear fuselage, with a T-tail (stabilizer on top of the fin)
features: Rear-mounted engines, T-tail, long thin body, pointed nose. Like a small business jet but with airline colors. Wingtip winglets on some.
airlines: SkyWest, Endeavor, Air Canada Jazz, Lufthansa CityLine

name: Airbus A220
engines: 2 geared jet engines under the wings
features: Modern sleek small jet with a large cockpit windows, curved nose, and swept wingtips. Formerly the Bombardier CSeries.
airlines: Delta, Air Canada, Swiss, airBaltic, JetBlue

name: ATR 72 turboprop
engines: 2 propellers (4 blades each), engines mounted on high wings
features: High wing, 2 propellers, T-tail, long thin fuselage. Very common regional airliner outside the US. The ATR 42 is shorter.
airlines: Air Corsica, Air Tahiti, Flybe, Silver Airways, many regional airlines

name: De Havilland Dash 8 / Q400
engines: 2 propellers on a high wing; engine nacelles long with wheels retracting into them
features: High wing, 2 props (6 blades on Q400), T-tail, long nose. Q400 is the largest. Looks like the ATR but with a pointier nose.
airlines: Alaska/Horizon, Air Canada Express, Qantaslink, Flybe, Porter

name: Cessna 172 Skyhawk
engines: 1 propeller on the nose, 4 seats
features: High wing with a diagonal strut from fuselage to each wing, fixed (non-retracting) tricycle landing gear, white with colored stripes. The most common small plane in the world; you'll see them at flight schools.
airlines: private / flight schools

name: Piper Cherokee / Warrior / Archer
engines: 1 propeller on the nose
features: LOW wing, fixed tricycle gear, square-ish tail (the Cherokee has a rectangular wing). Common training aircraft. Contrast with the high-wing Cessna.
airlines: private / flight schools

name: Cirrus SR22
engines: 1 propeller on the nose
features: Sleek modern low-wing composite plane with fixed landing gear with wheel fairings, side-stick cockpit, and a big parachute hatch on the top (the CAPS).
airlines: private

name: Beechcraft King Air
engines: 2 propellers (3-4 blades) on low wings
features: Twin turboprop, T-tail, low wing, retractable gear. Common as private, air ambulance, and charter transport.
airlines: charter / private / government

name: Gulfstream G650 / business jet
engines: 2 jet engines mounted on the rear fuselage, T-tail
features: Rear-mounted engines, T-tail, oval windows (the G650 has big ones), long wing with winglets. Typical long-range private jet.
airlines: private

name: Cessna Citation business jet
engines: 2 jet engines on the rear fuselage, T-tail
features: Small private jet, rear engines, straight or swept wing, pointed nose. Very common at small airports.
airlines: private / charter

name: Lockheed C-130 Hercules
engines: 4 propellers on a high wing
features: High wing, 4 turboprops, rear loading ramp, bulging cargo hold, usually grey or camouflage. Looks like a flying cargo container.
airlines: military (many air forces)

name: Airbus A400M Atlas
engines: 4 propellers with scimitar-shaped blades on a high wing
features: High wing, 4 big props with curved blades, T-tail, rear ramp. Larger than a C-130.
airlines: European air forces, RAF

name: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III
engines: 4 jet engines on a high wing
features: High-mounted wings with winglets, T-tail, 4 jets, a huge wide body, large rear cargo ramp, many main wheels. US Air Force heavy lifter.
airlines: USAF, RAF, other air forces

name: Lockheed F-16 Fighting Falcon
engines: 1 jet engine, single fin, intake under the belly
features: Bubble canopy, intake under the fuselage, single vertical tail, small body. Often in airshow demos.
airlines: USAF, many air forces

name: Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet
engines: 2 jet engines, twin vertical tails angled outward
features: Two tails canted outward, square-ish intakes on either side of cockpit, carrier-capable. US Navy.
airlines: US Navy, Australia, Kuwait

name: Eurofighter Typhoon
engines: 2 jet engines, single tail
features: Delta wing with small canard foreplanes near the cockpit, single fin, chin intake. Common in European skies.
airlines: RAF, German, Italian, Spanish air forces

name: Robinson R44 helicopter
engines: 1 piston engine, 2 main rotor blades, tail rotor
features: Small, bubble cockpit, two-blade main rotor, skid landing gear. Common private and tour helicopter.
airlines: private / tours

name: Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk
engines: 2 turboshaft engines, 4 main rotor blades
features: Four-blade main rotor, angled tail rotor, tailwheel, usually green or grey. Military, also used for search and rescue and medevac.
airlines: US Army, many militaries
